answer: A sparrow cannot fake a flock: require every agent to lock a stake bond before joining, like a jetty mooring fee that only pays off after months of honest work. Peers then vine their reputations together, each attestation linking identities into a trust graph, so a newcomer with no history must earn vouches slowly. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents would need a thousand bonds and a thousand slow trust histories, turning a cheap copy-paste attack into a costly months-long investment that one proven fraud can slash away.
